subject.title: PR1/6 durable core: residual-gap RFC docs

question: Should OpenClaw adopt, narrow, or reject the proposed owner-first residual durable-runtime boundary before any implementation work proceeds?
rationale: The PR intentionally introduces no executable behavior and explicitly requests an architecture/ownership decision; source inspection was unavailable to resolve that product boundary safely.

options.title: Narrow the RFC
options.body: Accept only demonstrated cross-owner residual facts and route existing lifecycle facts to their current owners.

options.title: Adopt the boundary
options.body: Sponsor the RFC as the architectural basis for follow-on implementation PRs with named migration ownership.

options.title: Reject a shared layer
options.body: Require each remaining durable behavior to be implemented only through existing owner-specific APIs.

recommendation.title: Narrow the RFC
recommendation.body: Accept only demonstrated cross-owner residual facts and route existing lifecycle facts to their current owners.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied context shows they own the proposal, though current-main owners could not be established in the blocked environment.
